summary: Implemented typed Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI adapter APIs for detection, manifest-driven install, drift status, targeted repair, safe uninstall, recovery, and context bootstrap. D-032 through D-034 add trusted three-factor mutation authority, complete native source sets, and kit-authored target-flavored bridges. All required validation commands pass.
behavior_implemented: Typed independent Codex, Claude, and Gemini detection using injected executable discovery, project markers, capability reports, and fail-safe supported-version ranges.
Repository-first canonical skill and registry loading with a deterministic packaged-agent-kit fallback and registry-derived side-effect advisories.
Generated and native-verified manifest entries, typed instruction-bridge and MCP components, producer validation, project-local backup records, and legacy generated-manifest compatibility.

D-032 three-factor overwrite and deletion authority: an adapter-scoped schema-valid path, current bytes equal to the manifest-recorded hash, and the exact raw manifest digest authenticated by the fixed per-project Work Context user-configuration install record.

Trusted pending transitions bind client, manifest path, prior and next manifest digests, and the ordered operation digest; authority is rechecked after transaction intent persistence and immediately before every apply or recovery mutation.

D-033 complete native-verified source sets with sorted canonical-path and sha256 pairs for every file below a skill directory plus a domain-separated aggregate digest; add, remove, rename, and content drift are detected.

D-034 self-contained, target-flavored bridge templates authored in the packaged kit; synchronization covers only skills and registry, context AGENTS content is preserved, and bridges are generated only when absent.

Content-hash-idempotent install, drift status, targeted repair, manifest-listed-only uninstall, process locking, atomic replacement, and durable recovery; any failed authority factor makes the whole plan report-only.
Typed open_context subprocess bootstrap without credential handling.
MCP status reported exactly as not_implemented without server identity or configuration generation.
No-follow project-scoped filesystem operations and negative tests proving client authentication credentials and user-global client auth files are never read, copied, configured, or required.

tests.result: Success: no issues found in 79 source files

tests.command: Audit git status --porcelain=v1 -uall against contract allowed_paths
tests.result: Allowed-path audit passed for all 80 changed files.

assumptions: The operator's Round 2 and Round 3 instructions for the revision worktree, branch, and base supersede stale location metadata in contract.json; allowed and forbidden path grants remain unchanged.
The fixed platformdirs Work Context user-configuration location is the trusted domain required by D-032 and is distinct from prohibited client authentication and client-global configuration files.
MCP configuration generation remains a deliberate D-014 non-goal until WP-330 defines the server identity.
decisions: D-026: Codex uses native-verified manifest entries while generated outputs use explicit generated entries.
D-027: canonical skills and registry ship in a deterministically synchronized package resource kit.
D-028: selected-client bridges are generated only when absent; existing user bridges remain untouched.
D-029: Gemini uses .gemini/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and every client probe uses a declared supported-version range with fail-safe unsupported results.
D-030: retained backups are project-local under .workctx/backups/<timestamp>/ and manifest-listed.

D-032: overwrite or deletion requires adapter-scoped path authority, target hash equality, and a project-manifest digest authenticated by the fixed user-directory install record; otherwise the entire plan is report-only.
D-033: native-verified entries record sorted complete source sets plus an aggregate digest.
D-034: bridge templates are self-contained and kit-authored; source synchronization covers only skills and registry, and context AGENTS remains the base contract.
D-014: MCP configuration generation is deferred until WP-330.
security_considerations: The only user-configuration artifact accessed is Work Context's own fixed agent-adapter install record, whose public API has no path override; no client auth file, token, credential, or client-global configuration is accessed.
The exact raw manifest digest and current target hash are revalidated against the trusted record after transaction intent persistence and immediately before every target mutation or recovery write.

Adapter targets and native source paths are allowlisted and project-relative; no-follow access rejects traversal, symlinks or reparse points, unsafe Windows names, case collisions, and credential-capable names before content access.

Existing user bridges and all unauthenticated or modified targets remain untouched; uninstall removes only authenticated manifest-listed generated targets and never recursively removes neighboring user content.
Tests use isolated fake project and home directories plus fake executable discovery, so no real client or real user-global auth file is required.
MCP has a data-only not_implemented seam with no server identity, configuration target, or credential path.
migration_considerations: Readers accept legacy generated manifests while current writers emit explicit modes, typed components, and complete native source sets.

Successful adapter operations create or update the separate trusted install record in Work Context's fixed user-configuration location; uninstall removes the applicable trusted record without inspecting or migrating client-global state.
Transaction preimages and manifest bookkeeping use retained project-local backups; no user-global backup migration occurs.
recommended_next_action: Lead review and integration, followed by separately owned CLI wiring; WP-330 may later implement the reserved MCP seam with its defined server identity.
